## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized dung beetle characterized by a rounded dark body, strong digging legs, and the habit of shaping and rolling dung into balls. In Florida, the Eastern Tumblebug is found in pastures, prairies, fields, sandy open areas, pine flatwoods, roadsides, and other habitats where mammal dung is available. Adults and larvae feed on dung, with adults rolling or burying dung balls as brood provisions, helping recycle nutrients, improve soil structure, and remove waste from the landscape.
